statement: The function returns a result r (not a failure), and r = true if and only if there exists a finite list c_1, ..., c_k containing exactly the distinct color values that occur in targetGrid, each once, such that: for every p with 1 <= p <= k, and every cell (i,j) in the bounding box of c_p (that is, minRow(c_p) <= i <= maxRow(c_p) and minCol(c_p) <= j <= maxCol(c_p), where minRow(c), maxRow(c), minCol(c), maxCol(c) are the minimum and maximum row and column indices of cells of color c in targetGrid), if targetGrid[i][j] != c_p then the color targetGrid[i][j] occurs later in the list, i.e. there is q with p < q <= k and c_q = targetGrid[i][j].
preconditions: targetGrid is a valid grid: writing m = len(targetGrid) and n = len(targetGrid[0]), 1 <= m <= 60, 1 <= n <= 60, every row of targetGrid has length n, and 1 <= targetGrid[i][j] <= 60 for every 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n.

statement: There is a Boolean r such that is_printable(targetGrid) returns r; equivalently, the call does not fail (no panic, overflow, or out-of-bounds).
preconditions: targetGrid is a valid grid: writing m = len(targetGrid) and n = len(targetGrid[0]), 1 <= m <= 60, 1 <= n <= 60, every row of targetGrid has length n, and 1 <= targetGrid[i][j] <= 60 for every 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n.

statement: The function returns a result r and r = true.
preconditions: targetGrid is a valid grid: writing m = len(targetGrid) and n = len(targetGrid[0]), 1 <= m <= 60, 1 <= n <= 60, every row of targetGrid has length n, and 1 <= targetGrid[i][j] <= 60 for every 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n. Also, there exists a color c such that targetGrid[i][j] = c for every 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n.

statement: Whenever the function returns r = true, there exists a color c occurring in targetGrid such that every cell in the bounding box of c has color c: for every i,j with minRow(c) <= i <= maxRow(c) and minCol(c) <= j <= maxCol(c), targetGrid[i][j] = c, where minRow(c), maxRow(c), minCol(c), maxCol(c) are the minimum and maximum row and column indices of cells of color c in targetGrid.
preconditions: targetGrid is a valid grid: writing m = len(targetGrid) and n = len(targetGrid[0]), 1 <= m <= 60, 1 <= n <= 60, every row of targetGrid has length n, and 1 <= targetGrid[i][j] <= 60 for every 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n.

statement: Whenever the function returns r = true, there exists a color c occurring in targetGrid such that no other occurring color d != c has a cell of color c inside the bounding box of d. Explicitly, for every occurring color d != c and every position (i,j) with targetGrid[i][j] = c, it is not the case that minRow(d) <= i <= maxRow(d) and minCol(d) <= j <= maxCol(d), where minRow(x), maxRow(x), minCol(x), maxCol(x) are the minimum and maximum row and column indices of cells of color x.
preconditions: targetGrid is a valid grid: writing m = len(targetGrid) and n = len(targetGrid[0]), 1 <= m <= 60, 1 <= n <= 60, every row of targetGrid has length n, and 1 <= targetGrid[i][j] <= 60 for every 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n.

statement: The function returns a result r and r = false.
preconditions: targetGrid is a valid grid: writing m = len(targetGrid) and n = len(targetGrid[0]), 1 <= m <= 60, 1 <= n <= 60, every row of targetGrid has length n, and 1 <= targetGrid[i][j] <= 60 for every 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n. Also, there exist distinct colors a and b occurring in targetGrid such that the bounding box of a contains at least one cell whose target color is b, and the bounding box of b contains at least one cell whose target color is a.

statement: Whenever the function returns r = false, there exist an integer k >= 2 and distinct colors c_1, ..., c_k occurring in targetGrid such that, setting c_{k+1} = c_1, for every p with 1 <= p <= k the bounding box of c_p contains at least one cell whose targetGrid color is c_{p+1}. Here the bounding box of a color x is the smallest rectangle of positions containing every occurrence of x.
preconditions: targetGrid is a valid grid: writing m = len(targetGrid) and n = len(targetGrid[0]), 1 <= m <= 60, 1 <= n <= 60, every row of targetGrid has length n, and 1 <= targetGrid[i][j] <= 60 for every 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n.

statement: For every injective function f from the set of color values occurring in targetGrid into {1,2,...,60}, let targetGrid' be the same-shaped grid with targetGrid'[i][j] = f(targetGrid[i][j]) for all i,j. Whenever is_printable(targetGrid) returns r and is_printable(targetGrid') returns r', we have r = r'.

statement: The function returns a result r and r = false. This is the converse of spec_7 and generalizes S7: any directed cycle of bounding-box containments is an obstruction to printability.
preconditions: targetGrid is a valid grid: writing m = len(targetGrid) and n = len(targetGrid[0]), 1 <= m <= 60, 1 <= n <= 60, every row of targetGrid has length n, and 1 <= targetGrid[i][j] <= 60 for every 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n.
